items.title: Group-like p-form global symmetry and backgrounds
items.design_state: Codimension-general topological-defect prerequisite is current and ready. Direct dependency corrected from the supplier codimension-one interface definition; owner escalation is recorded for this cross-batch edge change.
items.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$, an integer $p$ with $0\le p<d$, and a smooth $d$-dimensional spacetime manifold $M$, possibly with boundary. A selected model $\mathcal T$ specifies its spacetime structure and boundary conditions; field configuration space, field bundles, regularity and admitted sectors; observables and their supports; normalized correlation functionals; and, when present, its action, regulator, measure, unit system and charge normalization. No such data are inferred from a familiar theory name.

Use the preceding topological-defect definition with its exact content: a defect is model-specified field, operator or boundary-condition data on a closed embedded support, and it is topological when every declared correlator is invariant under each admissible isotopy that transports its data, avoids other insertions and preserves boundary data. For this symmetry, each defect is an endodefect insertion in the same selected model; the model supplies parallel fusion and the induced action on its admitted observables and backgrounds. A support $\Sigma$ is the image of a smooth embedding $\iota:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M^\circ$ from a manifold without boundary, with closed image in the interior $M^\circ$.

A **group-like $p$-form global symmetry** of $\mathcal T$ consists of a locally compact Hausdorff topological group $G$ and an assignment $g\mapsto U_g(\Sigma)$ of invertible topological symmetry defects to the allowed closed supports $\Sigma$ of dimension $d-p-1$ and codimension $p+1$. The model must define the parallel fusion operation and a transparent identity defect, with $U_e(\Sigma)=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}$ and $U_g(\Sigma)\star U_h(\Sigma)=U_{gh}(\Sigma)$ whenever that fusion is defined. Each $U_g$ has a two-sided inverse $U_{g^{-1}}$ under the supplied fusion law, and crossing it induces an automorphism preserving the declared observables, backgrounds and correlators. The group $G$ is **effective**: elements inducing identical actions in every admitted correlator and on every admitted observable and background are identified. A group element labels a transformation, not the charge of an observable.

A **genuine $p$-dimensional observable** is an observable supported on a closed embedded $p$-dimensional submanifold whose definition is independent of an attached higher-dimensional support. Its symmetry action is defined by moving a symmetry defect across it, with the model specifying the resulting junction or operator action. For $p>0$, if crossing by every $U_g$ preserves the one-dimensional space $\mathbb C O$ for a nonzero genuine observable $O$, write the scalar action as $\chi_O(g)O$. If the resulting map $\chi_O:G\to U(1)$ is a continuous homomorphism in a model where $G$ is Abelian, call $\chi_O$ the character charge of $O$; it is an element of $\widehat G$. This definition does not assert scalarity, continuity or multiplicativity for every observable. For $p=0$, local observables may carry higher-dimensional representations of a non-Abelian group; the representation label is distinct from the group element implementing a transformation. For a locally compact Hausdorff Abelian group $A$, write its character group as $\widehat A=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}(A,U(1))$, with pointwise multiplication. Here $U(1)=\{e^{i\alpha}:\alpha\in\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z\}$, so every character value and its argument are dimensionless.

A **background** for a symmetry is nondynamical model data, not summed over. For a finite Abelian group $A$, fix a triangulation $K$ of $M$ and let $C^k(K;A)$ be the group of functions from oriented $k$-simplices to $A$, with orientation reversal acting by negation. Its coboundary is the alternating sum over faces,

$$
(\delta c)([v_0,\ldots,v_{k+1}])=\sum_{j=0}^{k+1}(-1)^j c([v_0,\ldots,\widehat v_j,\ldots,v_{k+1}]).
$$

Since $\delta^2=0$ by pairwise cancellation of twice-deleted faces, a discrete $(p+1)$-form background with no higher-group mixing is a cocycle $B\in C^{p+1}(K;A)$ modulo $B\mapsto B+\delta\Lambda$ for $\Lambda\in C^p(K;A)$. Relative cochains or boundary-fixed gauge transformations are used when required by the model's boundary conditions. If other backgrounds mix with $B$, the model must give the modified cocycle and gauge-transformation laws.

For a continuous $U(1)^r$ $p$-form symmetry, a background consists of model-supplied local $(p+1)$-form potentials, their overlap and lower-overlap transition data, a globally specified curvature locally given by $H=dB$, and the small and large gauge transformations with their holonomy and integral-flux normalization. Small transformations have the local form $B\mapsto B+d\Lambda$ for a $p$-form $\Lambda$. The unit system and all coefficients in background couplings remain model inputs. The model must define its correlators in these backgrounds; this definition asserts neither that every symmetry admits such a coupling nor that the symmetry can be gauged.
items.physical_scope: A kinematic definition for a named d-dimensional model with model-defined fields, correlators, symmetry defects and background sectors; it asserts no continuum QFT existence, anomaly absence, universal background coupling, or gauging.

items.title: Exchangeability makes p-form symmetry groups Abelian and simple charges characters
items.design_state: Complete conditional proof authored; its p-form definition prerequisite is current and ready.
items.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $1\le p<d$, and let $\mathcal T$ have a group-like $p$-form global symmetry $G$ as defined above. Assume the selected model has a unitary Hilbert-space realization and, for every $g,h\in G$, admits two parallel copies of their codimension-$(p+1)$ symmetry supports inside a contractible neighborhood with a disk spanned by two independent normal directions, together with an isotopy exchanging their order without intersecting any other insertion or changing boundary data. Then $G$ is Abelian.

Let $O(C)$ be a nonzero genuine $p$-dimensional operator bounded in the operator norm of the selected Hilbert-space representation. Call it **simple for this result** when each topological local junction endomorphism on $O$ produced by passing a symmetry defect across it is a scalar multiple of $O$. Assume the induced action on the one-dimensional space spanned by $O$ is continuous and unitary. There is a continuous character $\chi_O:G\to U(1)$ such that passing $U_g$ across $O$ multiplies it by $\chi_O(g)$. Thus the charge of $O$ belongs to the Pontryagin dual $\widehat G=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,U(1))$. This theorem makes no claim for $p=0$ or for operators with nonscalar crossing endomorphisms.
items.physical_scope: A conditional result for one group-like symmetry in a unitary selected model whose codimension-greater-than-one defects admit the stated local exchange isotopies; simple bounded charged operators are considered only when their crossing action is scalar.

references.locator: §3, PDF pp. 11–12: group-like defect fusion, exchangeability for q>0, and the qualifications on topology.

references.title: Lakshya Bhardwaj et al., Lectures on Generalized Symmetries
references.locator: §§2.2.1–2.2.2, PDF pp. 12–20: Abelianity by exchanging topological defects, simple p-dimensional operators, characters, and the Pontryagin dual charge group.

title: Higher-Form Symmetries and Charge Operators — Examples

items.title: Magnetic one-form charge of an external U(1) line
items.design_state: The field-configuration proof derives the U(1) character directly from the integer flux data, so it does not import the abstract theorem or assume that the line satisfies its Hilbert-space simplicity hypotheses.
items.statement:
Use natural units $\hbar=c=1$ and $M=\mathbb R^4$ with its standard orientation and Euclidean metric. The selected field model is pure compact Maxwell theory with actual gauge group $U(1)=\{e^{i\alpha}:\alpha\in\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z\}$, no dynamical electric or magnetic matter, and a smooth right principal $U(1)$-bundle with connection on the complement of admitted external line insertions. A principal connection is a smooth $\mathfrak u(1)$-valued one-form reproducing each fundamental vertical vector and equivariant under the right group action. Identify $\mathfrak u(1)=i\mathbb R$ with $\mathbb R$ so its local potentials $A_i$ have holonomy $\exp(i\int A_i)$ and the real curvature $F$ obeys $F|_{U_i}=dA_i$, since the Abelian Lie bracket vanishes. The model fixes the action convention $S[A]=(2e^2)^{-1}\int F\wedge *F$ with dimensionless $e>0$, integrating outside any prescribed line-core tube with its declared boundary condition. It also fixes the allowed bundle sectors, boundary behavior at infinity, and any regulator or measure; no continuum measure is constructed here. With this normalization $[A_i]=\mathrm{length}^{-1}$, $[F]=\mathrm{length}^{-2}$, and $\int_\Sigma F$ is dimensionless.

Let $C$ be a closed smooth oriented curve carrying an admitted genuine external magnetic line $T_m(C)$, where genuine means that no auxiliary surface is attached to define the insertion. Its integer charge $m\in\mathbb Z$ is specified by $\int_{S^2_{\mathrm{link}}}F=2\pi m$ on every sufficiently small oriented normal two-sphere linking $C$. The model has no other magnetic sources, and its normalized correlation functional is assumed to be defined for these insertions.

For a closed smooth oriented surface $\Sigma$ disjoint from the line, and $\alpha\in\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$, define the magnetic surface operator

$$
U_\alpha(\Sigma)=\exp\!\left(\frac{i\alpha}{2\pi}\int_\Sigma F\right).
$$

For this example, a smooth singular three-chain is a finite real linear combination of smooth maps from the standard 3-simplex, with boundary the alternating sum of its face maps. For a source-free move, the model supplies a compact smooth singular three-chain $V$ in $M\setminus C$ with $\partial V=\Sigma_1-\Sigma_0$. For a move across the line, the model supplies a compact oriented smooth three-dimensional track $W$ in $M$, represented as a finite smooth singular chain, with endpoint boundary $\partial W=\Sigma_1-\Sigma_0$; its support is a smooth embedded three-manifold near each of its finitely many intersections with $C$, and the intersections are transverse interior points. Transverse means that the tangent space of this three-manifold and the tangent line of $C$ span $T_xM$. Excise a small open three-ball in each such regular neighborhood. The model supplies a source-free collar in the punctured tubular neighborhood identifying each resulting boundary sphere with a small oriented normal two-sphere $S_j^2$ linking $C$. The resulting punctured chain $V$ lies in $M\setminus C$ and has $\partial V=\Sigma_1-\Sigma_0-\sum_j\epsilon_jS_j^2$, where $\epsilon_j$ is the oriented intersection sign of $W$ with $C$. Define the algebraic intersection number $I(W,C)=\sum_j\epsilon_j$. The claimed action is that a source-free move leaves $U_\alpha$ unchanged, while a move across the line multiplies it by $e^{i\alpha m I(W,C)}$. In particular, the line carries the character $\chi_m(e^{i\alpha})=e^{i\alpha m}$ of the magnetic one-form $U(1)$ symmetry.
items.physical_scope: A conditional field-configuration example for a pure compact U(1) Maxwell model in four Euclidean dimensions with an external genuine magnetic line; it makes no continuum-measure, empirical, or general interacting-QFT claim.

references.title: Davide Gaiotto, Anton Kapustin, Nathan Seiberg, and Brian Willett, Generalized Global Symmetries
references.locator: §4.1, PDF pp. 14–16: pure U(1) gauge theory, the magnetic one-form current F/(2π), the magnetic surface operator, its 2π periodicity, and charged 't Hooft loops.

items.title: A non-Abelian zero-form symmetry and its representation labels
items.design_state: Complete finite-model verification authored; the p-form and character-theorem suppliers are current and ready.
items.statement:
Let $M=S^1_\beta$ be Euclidean time of circumference $\beta>0$, let $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^3$ with orthonormal basis $e_1,e_2,e_3$, and let the Hamiltonian be $H_0=0$. Use natural units $\hbar=1$. The finite model's normalized correlation functional for time-ordered operator insertions is $C(O_1,\ldots,O_n)=\frac13\operatorname{Tr}(O_1\cdots O_n)$. Let $S_3$ be the group of permutations of $\{1,2,3\}$, with composition $(\sigma\tau)(j)=\sigma(\tau(j))$, and define the unitary action $\rho(\sigma)e_j=e_{\sigma(j)}$. A symmetry defect at time $t$ is $U_\sigma(t)=\rho(\sigma)$.

The state space decomposes as $\mathcal H=\mathbb C(e_1+e_2+e_3)\oplus V_2$, where $V_2=\{(z_1,z_2,z_3)\in\mathbb C^3:z_1+z_2+z_3=0\}$. The first summand is the trivial representation and $V_2$ is the two-dimensional standard irreducible representation. The representation label of a state sector is therefore either the trivial representation or the standard two-dimensional representation; a permutation $\sigma\in S_3$ is instead a group element implementing a symmetry transformation. This is an ordinary $p=0$ example and does not conflict with the exchange theorem for $p\ge1$.
items.physical_scope: A finite three-state quantum-mechanical system with a unitary S3 zero-form symmetry; the representation decomposition is exact for this finite model and makes no field-theory or empirical claim.
